problem: Rewrite the expression $({x}^{2}-10x+25)+1$ as the sum of a perfect square and a constant.

feedback.problem: Rewrite the expression $({y}^{2}-4y+4)+1$ as the sum of a perfect square and a constant.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{y}^{2}-2ay+{a}^{2}=(y-a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-4y+4 & = \\ {y}^{2}-4y+{2}^{2} & = \\ {y}^{2}-2\cdot 2y+{2}^{2} & = \\ (y-2{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}^{2}-4y+4)+1 & = \\ (y-2{)}^{2}+1 & .\end{aligned}
$$
